topic: How Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) Store Facts in Transformers

sections.title: The Analogy: The Brain vs. The Library
lecture_lines: Attention layers act as a flexible search engine.
MLP layers provide the model's long-term memory.
Attention gathers relevant context for a token.
MLP provides facts stored within its parameters.
Together, they form a reasoning engine. [Asset: AnalogyDiagram]

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Key-Value Projection
lecture_lines: MLP layers consist of two linear transformations.
Non-linear activations bridge these linear projections.
This architecture functions as a pattern matcher. [Asset: GridConstellation]

sections.title: Mechanism: Key-Value Memory Networks
lecture_lines: Each neuron acts as a specific template.
The first layer acts as a key.
The second layer acts as a value. [Asset: MemoryNetworkDiagram]
animations: Animate input mapping to Key matrix in #FFFF00.

sections.title: Visualizing Fact Retrieval
lecture_lines: We represent MLP transformation as a function.
Input patterns match via the first weight.
Fact injection occurs through the second weight.
The signal flows through a bottleneck.
Facts are distributed across these weights. [Asset: MathFlowDiagram]

sections.title: Conclusion: Distributed Representation
lecture_lines: Facts exist as distributed synaptic memories.
Erasing single neurons doesn't destroy total knowledge.
Weights collectively encode the model's reality. [Asset: WeightsDistributionGraph]
